Class a run's issues

Source: R/lineage_classify.R
gpq_classify_issues.Rd

Gives each issue its class, source (the provider's to fix), harmonization (made by the pipeline that converted the data) or unclassified, and says what decided it. The issues' issue_class and class_basis are set by reference.

Usage

gpq_classify_issues(
  issues,
  rules,
  evidence = list(),
  overrides = NULL,
  settings = list()
)

Arguments

issues

The issues table of a run's results, from gpq_check_conformance(): a data.table, changed by reference.

rules

NULL, or the rule set the run used, such as magp_rules() returns: its rules rows give rules their classes, and its settings rows can give fallback_class.

evidence

A named list of evidence tables for issues whose class is depends, each a data.frame or the path of a CSV file: computed, filled, lineage and crosswalk (see Details).

overrides

NULL, or your overrides: a data.frame or the path of a CSV file with the columns fingerprint, rule_id, table_name, column_name, issue_class (source or harmonization), who, when and why, and any of the issues' group columns, each row giving at least one of the scope cells. gpq_preflight() checks them when given as its input overrides.

settings

A named list of settings, which come before the rule set's, the options' and the built-in values (see groundplotqc_options). It reads fallback_class, classes by rule ID, such as c(some_rule = "source"). The first of those that gives fallback_class gives all of it: an argument naming one rule replaces every entry of the rule set's row or the option, so the other rules have none.

Value

issues, invisibly, with issue_class and class_basis set.

Details

Each issue first takes its rule's class, with class_basis "default": the class of the most specific row of the rule set's rules that gives one, else the class the rule is registered with. An information rule's class is "none".

Your overrides then class any issue, whatever its rule's class. An override gives a class to the issues whose cells match every scope cell it gives: fingerprint (the issue's fingerprint or fingerprint_pk), rule_id, table_name, column_name and any group column; a blank cell matches every issue. Where several overrides match an issue, the most specific wins, in this order: a fingerprint; a rule, column and group; a rule and column; a rule and group; a rule; a column and group; a column; a group; a table alone. Within each, an override naming the table comes before one that doesn't, and one group column or several count alike. Two overrides of the winning kind that give different classes leave the issue unclassified, with class_basis "override conflict"; otherwise class_basis is "override". An override naming a rule that was renamed or split applies to its new rules.

Then an issue whose reason_code is harmonization_artifact is harmonization, with class_basis "reason code", unless an override classed it or left it in conflict.

Then the evidence settles an issue whose class is still depends as harmonization, the first of these tables to settle it giving class_basis:

  • computed: columns the pipeline computes, with the columns table_name, column_name, derivation (id, class, formula, count, fill or reference) and one group column of the issues, which gives the group value the row is for, "*" for every value. An issue on such a column in that group, of a record or of the whole column, is "computed".

  • filled: cells the pipeline's missing-value fill wrote (table_name, record_pk, column_name, written_value). An issue on such a cell whose value is the one written is "filled".

  • lineage, the provider's raw values of the cells the pipeline changed (table_name, record_pk, column_name, raw_value, raw_source), with crosswalk, each provider code and the code it is translated to (provider_code, code, column_name and one group column of the issues). Together they settle a record's code_not_in_list issue, whose raw value is its cell's raw_value, or its own value where lineage doesn't list the cell. Where crosswalk has rows for the issue's column and group value, a raw value listed there as a provider_code makes it "lineage": the provider's code was valid. A raw value not listed there makes it "crosswalk" only where the pipeline changed the cell, that is where lineage lists the cell with a raw value other than its value; otherwise the issue stays unsettled, as does one whose column and group value crosswalk has no rows for.

A cell listed twice in filled or lineage stops classification.

An issue whose class is still depends takes the fallback_class setting's class for its rule (class_basis "fallback"), else it is unclassified (class_basis "default").

See also

gpq_check_conformance() for the issues, gpq_decode_lineage() for their provider keys, and gpq_preflight() for the checks of the overrides.

Examples

example <- function(file) system.file("extdata", "examples", file, package = "groundplotqc")
fish <- gpq_read_spec(
  dictionary = example("fish_dictionary.csv"),
  code_lists = list(
    water_body = example("fish_water_body.csv"), gear = example("fish_gear.csv"),
    species = example("fish_species.csv")
  ),
  column_map = gpq_column_map(
    table = "table", attribute = "field", type = "kind", key_type = "key",
    reference = "parent", lookup = "codes", description = "notes",
    min_value = "low", max_value = "high", min_inclusive = "low_in",
    max_inclusive = "high_in", pattern = "format", max_length = "width",
    decimals = "places", units = "unit"
  ),
  type_map = gpq_type_map(example("fish_types.csv")),
  sentinels = gpq_sentinels(
    numeric = c(missing = -99, not_applicable = -88),
    character = c(missing = "?", not_applicable = "~"),
    date = c(missing = "?", not_applicable = "~")
  )
)
# A haul that fished 900 minutes, past the dictionary's 600, and a species code not in
# the species list.
tables <- list(
  stations = data.frame(
    station_id = "S1", station_name = "Long Lake", water_body = "LK", depth = 1.5,
    first_visit = "2020-06-01"
  ),
  hauls = data.frame(
    haul_id = c("H1", "H2"), station_id = "S1", gear = "GN", minutes = c(30L, 900L),
    haul_date = "2020-06-01"
  ),
  catches = data.frame(
    catch_id = c("C1", "C2"), haul_id = "H1", species = c("WAE", "XYZ"),
    fish_count = 3L, weight = 1.2
  )
)
results <- gpq_check_conformance(tables, fish, group_cols = "water_body", layers = 0:3)
# Your override: the long haul is the provider's to fix.
overrides <- data.frame(
  fingerprint = NA, rule_id = "value_above_max", table_name = "hauls",
  column_name = "minutes", issue_class = "source", who = "A. Reviewer",
  when = "2026-10-22", why = "The gear log gives 45 minutes."
)
gpq_classify_issues(results$issues, rules = NULL, overrides = overrides)
results$issues[, c("rule_id", "column_name", "value", "issue_class", "class_basis")]
#>             rule_id column_name  value  issue_class class_basis
#>              <char>      <char> <char>       <char>      <char>
#> 1: code_not_in_list     species    XYZ unclassified     default
#> 2:  value_above_max     minutes    900       source    override

# A fallback class for the code issues nothing else settles.
gpq_classify_issues(
  results$issues,
  rules = NULL, overrides = overrides,
  settings = list(fallback_class = c(code_not_in_list = "source"))
)
results$issues[, c("rule_id", "column_name", "value", "issue_class", "class_basis")]
#>             rule_id column_name  value issue_class class_basis
#>              <char>      <char> <char>      <char>      <char>
#> 1: code_not_in_list     species    XYZ      source    fallback
#> 2:  value_above_max     minutes    900      source    override
